cards.explanation: The answer is that God had blessed him. The text says, "For God had blessed Obed-edom." (1 Chronicles 26:5) Eight sons, and the passage hands the credit straight to God. I think that's a full house, friends, and I can barely keep one bakery stocked.
The answer is capable. The text says Shemaiah's sons "…ruled over their families because they were strong, capable men." (1 Chronicles 26:6) Strong and capable, and that's the reason given, friends.

The answer is True. The text says Shimri wasn't the firstborn, "…his father had appointed him as the first…" (1 Chronicles 26:10) Hosah made the call himself. Shimri got the first spot on the list because of his dad's choice.

The answer is that they cast lots for each gate. "They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike." (1 Chronicles 26:13) Every gate got its keeper by lot. Families, young and old alike, all got in on it. I think that kept everybody from arguing over the good spots.

The answer is False. The gatekeepers cast lots "…according to their families, young and old alike." (1 Chronicles 26:13) Young and old both got a turn, friends. I think that's the fairest way to hand out a job.

The answer is a wise counselor. The text calls Zechariah "…a wise counselor…" and the lot for the North Gate fell to him. (1 Chronicles 26:14) A man like that at the gate sounds like a good person to have around.

The answer is the storehouses. "The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses to his sons." (1 Chronicles 26:15) Dad got the gate and the sons got the storehouses. Sounds like a family business to me, bakers. Somebody get that family matching aprons.

The answer is at every watch. The text says, "There were guards stationed at every watch." (1 Chronicles 26:16) Every single watch gets a guard. Friends, I'd be the guy asking where the break room is.

The answer is True. The text sums up the list: "These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and Merari." (1 Chronicles 26:19) Korah and Merari, the two family lines behind all those gate posts.

The answer is the treasuries. "Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things." (1 Chronicles 26:20) The gates had their guards, and the treasuries had their own keepers. Different jobs, same house. Me, friends, I can barely guard one cookie jar.

The answer is Moses. The text says Shebuel was "…a descendant of Gershom son of Moses…" (1 Chronicles 26:24) Gershom's father is Moses. Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), so the officer over the treasuries comes from his line.

The answer is plunder from their battles. "They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD." (1 Chronicles 26:27) Some of what they won in battle went to the house of the LORD. They took part of their winnings and gave it away. Friends, I can't even give away the last cookie without a fight in my head.

The answer is True. "They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD." (1 Chronicles 26:27) Battle winnings, and some of them went to fixing up the place. I know a thing or two about needing repairs myself, bakers, so I like that.

The answer is judges. "…Chenaniah and his sons had the outside duties as officers and judges over Israel." (1 Chronicles 26:29) Outside duties, and the job titles are officers and judges. The missing word is the second one, friends.

The answer is that the records were searched. "In the fortieth year of David’s reign the records were searched, and strong, capable men were found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead." (1 Chronicles 26:31) The records are how they were found. I bet that search felt good once it paid off. That's a lot of reading, friends, and I would have lost my place twice.

The answer is False. King David appointed those men over the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh "…for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king." (1 Chronicles 26:32) They handled both, so the matters of God were in their care too. Both jobs, one group of men.
